ai.description: Giri’s ‘Brookiish’ Gecko (Gekkonidae) reaches 55 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal spots and a white venter. Distinctive features include a slender body and unkeeled, smooth ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus varadgirii* is best distinguished by its unique, non-tuberculate, smooth dorsal scales, which contrast with the heavily keeled or tubercular skin of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus varadgirii* inhabits the rocky outcrops and dry deciduous forests of the northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Giri’s ‘Brookiish’ gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus varadgirii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus varadgirii* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 300 and 1,200 meters.
